args.text: Electric vehicles produce fewer lifetime emissions than petrol cars even on coal-heavy grids. EV batteries lose most of their capacity within five years. Battery fires are more common in electric vehicles than in petrol cars.

status_means.not_research: only a record — a filing, a register or a news report — could settle this. Prism's research corpus has no opinion, and that is not the same as the claim being wrong
status_means.no_literature: no paper title matches this claim's own wording. The field may still cover it under different words — run research.evidence on the claim to find out
status_means.thin_literature: a handful of paper titles match this wording — too few to rest an assertion on without reading them
status_means.literature_exists: research exists on this subject — which is not the same as research agreeing with the claim; research.evidence reads it
status_means.claim_covered: papers cover BOTH sides of the claim, so the literature speaks to it directly
status_means.unchecked: the corpus lane failed for this claim

data.method: one model call extracts every claim and one the index scan counts them all, so a whole article costs two round trips. Matching is on the claim's OWN WORDING against paper titles — deliberately literal. research.evidence resolves a claim properly (naming its concepts, discovering the corpus's labels for them, reading abstracts) and will find work this screen misses. Use `deep` to run it here on the weakest claims.
data.evidence_coverage_means: share of the RESEARCH-CHECKABLE claims with a literature behind them, weighted by how directly it speaks to the claim. Claims only a record could settle are excluded rather than counted as failures. It is not a truth score: it says a body of work exists, not that the work agrees
data.citation_coverage_means: Not measured. Presence of a DOI or link does not verify a source or its support for a claim.

citations.verification_note: Corpus resolution is not publisher validation or proof of claim support. Unresolved does not mean fabricated.
citations.note: DOIs are tiered from the corpus; bare links are classified by host only, which is weaker evidence about a source's strength
